mappings.note: Structure of the uterus. A female reproductive organ described verbally, so LO-8; the drawn version of the female system later in the chapter adds C-5.1-LO-1, which is the rule used to split the two throughout.
What follows a successful human fertilisation, up to implantation. The fertilisation limb of LO-4; the frame has no implantation outcome, so LO-4 carries the whole item.
POOR FIT. Defines ovulation. No ovulation outcome exists. Not LO-8: the item asks for a process, not for the ovary as an organ, which is the rule separating this from the female-organ items.
POOR FIT. What causes menstruation. Same uncovered cycle territory as the other menstruation items; the competency is the ceiling.
POOR FIT. The term foetus from the ninth week. Gestation has no outcome in the frame.

POOR FIT. Maternal diet and foetal health. LO-10 was considered for its health clause and rejected: that clause qualifies the significance of contraceptive devices, and stretching it to antenatal nutrition would make LO-10 absorb every health sentence in the chapter.
A use of barrier methods, covering both pregnancy prevention and STI protection. The contraceptive-device limb of LO-10 in its cleanest form.

Names two STIs. Reaches LO-10 only through the fused reproductive-health clause; no STI outcome exists. Shares the outcome with the other STI items, which it can only be split from by which fact is recalled.
Full form and function of an IUD. The contraceptive-device limb of LO-10, exactly as written.

The principle behind oral contraceptive pills. Contraceptive-device limb again; this family of five device items honestly shares one outcome, because LO-10 is the only contraception code in the legal set.

POOR FIT. A characteristic of emotional maturity. Matches the two other maturity items on C5.2 (human life from the perspective of Social Sciences and Ethics); nothing biological is asked, so no C3 outcome applies.

POOR FIT. Louis Pasteur and life from pre-existing life. The scientist-attribution shape invites C6.1, LO-11 or LO-12, but Pasteur is not an Indian contribution, and the frame has no biogenesis outcome. Same call as the MCQ version of this item in part 2.

Defines an angiosperm by its sexual reproduction through flowers. Mapped to LO-8 because the defining feature is the flower, the plant's reproductive organ. Mild stretch: the frame has no outcome on plant groups.

Explains vegetative propagation (LO-7) and why it helps agriculture, which the answer gives as uniform identical offspring (LO-9). Both twins because the item has both halves, matching the farmer item in part 1.
Describes budding in hydra (LO-7) and asks why the offspring are called clones (LO-9). The second sub-question is what pulls in the heredity twin; the plain budding MCQ earlier takes LO-7 alone.
Spore formation in fungi and how it aids survival. LO-7 alone, because survival here is about dispersal and dormancy, not about genetic identity, so LO-9 is not engaged.
Meiosis maintains a constant chromosome number. Constancy, not variation, so the competency rather than C-3.3-LO-5 - the same call as the four other meiosis items.

Compares self and cross pollination on two axes: where pollen goes (LO-4) and whether an external agent is required (C-4.3-LO-1). The agent axis is what distinguishes this from the plain self-versus-cross items, which take LO-4 alone.
Traces stigma to seed, so it crosses the boundary between the two outcomes: pollination and fertilisation (LO-4), then ovule to seed (LO-3). Items that stop at the zygote take LO-4 alone.

External versus internal fertilisation plus the egg-number consequence. Both halves are the mode of fertilisation, so LO-4; this is the short-answer member of a family of five that shares the outcome.
POOR FIT. The role of the larval feeding stage. Post-fertilisation development is uncovered by every outcome in this frame.

POOR FIT. Traces an unfertilised egg from ovulation to menstruation. The whole journey is cycle physiology, which has no outcome; C-3.2-LO-4 was rejected precisely because fertilisation is stipulated not to happen.
Sperm and egg on size and motility, and where each is produced. The where-produced half anchors it on LO-8 (the reproductive organs); shares the outcome with the MCQ gamete-comparison item.

Two halves: why the lining thickens (no outcome exists) and what happens if fertilisation does occur (LO-4). Mapped on the second half because that is the half the frame can carry; the first half is a genuine gap.
Sequence from sperm entry to implantation. Pivots on fertilisation, so LO-4; identical outcome to the MCQ ordering version, which this family shares honestly.
